ownership: Parser and Config are separate actual native allocations. The aligned allocation prefix retains the original charged native memory owner; the parser's raw owner pointer is borrowed only from its own prefix.

Every real raw/string field block is allocated by the same actual allocator. A growth allocates and charges the replacement before releasing the old block; no capacity-derived approximate reservation exists.
Input is borrowed only during synchronous parse. Config owns its padded raw bytes and all copied selected fields; returned views borrow Config and remain valid after parser destruction.
An unpublished Config is held by unique_ptr with an exact native destructor. Every failure leaves output null; a published Config has exactly one transferred native owner.
The default type is a nonallocating private enum reflecting only the three original accepted strings. A missing field remains absent; an explicitly empty string remains present with length zero.

Every allocation failure is sticky in the active native Scope and then in Parser. The outer Zig owner must record the real native allocation-fatal event and retire this parser; parsing again is refused.

Parser allocation is performed at the original capacity/first-buffer boundary before iterate. This allows the actual producer flag to stop before the original unchecked missing string/development buffers could be dereferenced. The original raw-input BOM is removed only once by iterate.
algorithm: pad counts only the original four ASCII JSON whitespace characters, appends exactly the missing suffix, retains those raw bytes, and passes original length.
The actual simdjson ondemand grammar, UTF8, raw key comparison, iteration and error behavior remain in the pinned allocator successor; no replacement scanner is used.

The selected node_modules field loop preserves raw key matching, duplicate-field update behavior, ignored main conversion error, strict name/type handling, imports/exports object/array/string selection, and scripts object-only handling.
All field copies preserve explicit lengths, including embedded NUL. Raw object/array slices retain the original formatting emitted by value.raw_json().
